records.source: וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ כָּל־שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים וְיֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן־קָרֵ֔חַ וִֽיזַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן־הוֹשַֽׁעְיָ֑ה וְכָל־הָעָ֖ם מִקָּטֹ֥ן וְעַד־גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And approached all [the] commanders of the forces, and Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from small and unto great,
pieces: Then all the commanders of the forces came forward, including Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, with all the people from the least to the greatest.

L.1: Then all the commanders of the forces came near, with Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the small to the great,

R.1: Then all the army commanders came to Jeremiah. Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah were with them. All the people came too, from the least important to the most important.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the forces and Johanan: the officers who had gathered at Mizpah and rescued the captives from Ishmael
decisions.reason: These are the army officers who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah (40:7-8). After Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, Johanan and the commanders freed the people Ishmael had taken and brought them to Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, on the way to Egypt, because they feared what Babylon would do (41:11-18). This chapter goes on from there.

decisions.choice: Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, as the Hebrew reads here
alternatives: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, as the Hebrew reads at 43:2
Azariah, as the Greek translation reads here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names this leader Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah. In 43:2, where the same leaders reply to Jeremiah, the Hebrew has Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and the Greek translation (the Septuagint, where this chapter is chapter 49) is said to have Azariah here as well. The two names may belong to one man, or one form may have come in from the other in copying. A Jezaniah son of the Maacathite is named among the commanders in 40:8 (Jaazaniah in 2 Kings 25:23), but his father is not Hoshaiah, so he may be someone else. The Hebrew is followed. The description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: from the small to the great: everyone, whatever their rank
decisions.reason: The pair takes in the whole people, from the least important to the most important (6:13; 8:10; 2 Kings 25:26). The request comes from everyone, not from the leaders alone.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (Literal)
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 2, where the people speak. Balanced and Readable end the sentence here.

decisions.choice: came to Jeremiah; army commanders; least important to the most important
decisions.reason: Readable names Jeremiah, whom they approach (verse 2), and explains "small" and "great" as rank.

records.heading: The leaders ask for a word

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא תִּפָּל־נָ֤א תְחִנָּתֵ֨נוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְהִתְפַּלֵּ֤ל בַּעֲדֵ֨נוּ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּעַ֖ד כָּל־הַשְּׁאֵרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את כִּֽי־נִשְׁאַ֤רְנוּ מְעַט֙ מֵֽהַרְבֵּ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עֵינֶ֖יךָ רֹא֥וֹת אֹתָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: and they said to Jeremiah the prophet: let fall please our supplication before you, and pray for us to Yahweh your God for all the remnant the this, for we are left a few from many, as your eyes [are] seeing us,
pieces: They said to the prophet Jeremiah, "Please hear our request, and pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for us, for all this remnant. There were many of us, but only a few are left, as you can see for yourself.

L.2: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Please let our plea fall before you, and pray for us to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, for all this remnant; for we are left, a few out of many, as your eyes see us,

R.2: They said to the prophet Jeremiah, "Please listen to what we ask. Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for us, for all of us who are left. Once we were many, but now only a few of us are left, as you can see.

decisions.choice: let our plea fall before you: please accept our request
decisions.reason: A request is pictured as falling or being laid down before the person asked, as one bows before a superior. The same phrase is used for a plea to the king in 37:20 and 38:26, and for prayer to God in 36:7. The people show Jeremiah great respect.

decisions.choice: the LORD your God: the people speak of the LORD as Jeremiah's God
decisions.reason: They say "your God", as if the LORD were the prophet's God more than theirs. Jeremiah answers that he will pray to "your God", the God of all of them (verse 4), and in verse 6 the people say "the LORD our God". The shift of pronouns runs through the chapter and returns in verse 20.

decisions.choice: remnant: the few people left in Judah after the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word means what is left over. Here it is the small group that remained in the land after the exile of 586 BC and the murder of Gedaliah (40:11, 15). The prophets speak of a remnant both as the sign of a disaster and as the seed of hope (Isaiah 10:20-22).

decisions.choice: hear our request (B); listen to what we ask (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: There were many of us, but only a few are left
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "we are left a few from many" is unfolded into two clauses. Balanced and Readable end the sentence here, and verse 3 follows as a new sentence; Literal keeps one sentence with a comma.

records.source: וְיַגֶּד־לָ֨נוּ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֶת־הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֵֽלֶךְ־בָּ֑הּ וְאֶת־הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: so that may tell us Yahweh your God the way that we should go in it and the thing that we should do.
pieces: Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God tell us where we should go and what we should do."

L.3: so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God may tell us the way in which we should go, and the thing that we should do."

R.3: Ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to show us where we should go and what we should do."

decisions.choice: the way we should go and the thing we should do: both the road to take and the course of action
decisions.reason: "Way" can mean a literal road and also a way of life. Here both senses are close: the people are camped on the road to Egypt (41:17), and they ask which way to go and what to do.

decisions.choice: so that he may tell us: the purpose of the prayer
decisions.reason: The verb continues the request of verse 2. They ask Jeremiah to pray so that God will answer and make his will known.

decisions.choice: Let the LORD your God tell us (B); Ask the LORD your God to show us (R)
decisions.reason: Since Balanced and Readable ended verse 2 with a full stop, the purpose clause becomes its own request.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי הִנְנִ֧י מִתְפַּלֵּ֛ל אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם כְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֑ם וְֽהָיָ֡ה כָּֽל־הַדָּבָר֩ אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲנֶ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ אַגִּ֣יד לָכֶ֔ם לֹֽא־אֶמְנַ֥ע מִכֶּ֖ם דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And said to them Jeremiah the prophet: I have heard; look, I [am] praying to Yahweh your God according to your words, and it will be, every word that answers Yahweh you, I will tell to you; not I will withhold from you a word.
pieces: The prophet Jeremiah said to them, "I have heard you. I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God as you ask. Whatever {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answers, I will tell you; I will not keep back a single word from you."

L.4: And Jeremiah the prophet said to them, "I have heard. Look, I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God according to your words, and every word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answers you I will tell you; I will not hold back a word from you."

R.4: The prophet Jeremiah answered them, "I have heard you. I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God as you have asked. I will tell you everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answers. I will not hide anything from you."

decisions.choice: the LORD your God: Jeremiah says "your" to all of them, claiming the LORD as the people's God too
decisions.reason: The people said "your God" to Jeremiah alone (verse 2). Jeremiah answers with the plural "your": the LORD is the God of all of them, not only of the prophet. In verse 6 they take this up and say "our God".

decisions.choice: look, I am praying: I will pray now, as a promise
decisions.reason: The word "look" with a participle announces what the speaker is about to do. Jeremiah agrees at once.

decisions.choice: I will not hold back a word: I will tell everything, whether you like it or not
decisions.reason: The verb means to withhold or keep back. Jeremiah promises to tell them the whole answer, as God told him at his call (1:7, 17) and in 26:2. Verses 19-22 show that the answer was not the one they wanted.

decisions.choice: as you ask (B); as you have asked (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "according to your words" means doing what they have asked.

records.source: וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ אָמְר֣וּ אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ יְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔נוּ לְעֵ֖ד אֱמֶ֣ת וְנֶאֱמָ֑ן אִם־לֹ֡א כְּֽכָל־הַ֠דָּבָר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִֽשְׁלָחֲךָ֜ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And they said to Jeremiah: may be Yahweh against us as a witness of truth and faithful, if not according to all the word that sends you Yahweh your God to us, so we will do.
pieces: They said to Jeremiah, "If we fail to do all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God sends you to tell us, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be a true and faithful witness against us.

L.5: And they said to Jeremiah, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to every word with which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God sends you to us.

R.5: They said to Jeremiah, "If we do not do everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God sends you to tell us, may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be a true and faithful witness against us.

decisions.choice: may the LORD be a witness against us: a solemn oath calling on God to judge them if they break their word
decisions.reason: An oath called God to witness, so that he would punish the one who did not keep it (Genesis 31:50; 1 Samuel 12:5; Micah 1:2). The people bind themselves in the strongest way they can, and verses 20-21 hold them to it.

decisions.choice: true and faithful: a witness who will tell exactly what happened and can be relied on
decisions.reason: The two words come from the same root, which speaks of what is firm and reliable. Together they describe a witness who cannot be mistaken or bribed.

decisions.choice: if not ... so we will do: a promise in the form of an oath, "if we do not do it"
decisions.reason: Hebrew oaths often state the condition and leave the curse unspoken, or put it first as here: may God witness against us if we do not act. The sense is a firm promise to obey.

decisions.choice: the condition first: If we fail to do (B) / If we do not do (R) ..., may the LORD be ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the "if" clause before the oath, so the long sentence reads more easily; the sense is unchanged (m3).

records.source: אִם־ט֣וֹב וְאִם־רָ֔ע בְּק֣וֹל׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנַ֜חְנוּ שֹׁלְחִ֥ים אֹתְךָ֛ אֵלָ֖יו נִשְׁמָ֑ע לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִֽיטַב־לָ֔נוּ כִּ֣י נִשְׁמַ֔ע בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Whether good and whether bad, to [the] voice of Yahweh our God, whom we [are] sending you to him, we will listen, so that it may go well for us when we listen to [the] voice of Yahweh our God.
pieces: Whether we find it good or bad, we will obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to whom we are sending you. When we obey the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, it will go well with us."

L.6: Whether good or bad, we will listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."

R.6: Whether we like the answer or not, we will obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We are sending you to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If we obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, things will go well for us."

decisions.choice: whether good or bad: whether the answer pleases us or not
decisions.reason: Good and bad here describe how the answer will seem to them, welcome or unwelcome. The pair means "whatever it is".

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the LORD: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what he says (7:23; 26:13). The phrase frames the verse, and verse 21 says they did not do it.

decisions.choice: we: the full form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a short form of the word "we", found only rarely; the scribes marked the usual longer form to be read aloud (qere). Both mean the same.

decisions.choice: so that it may go well with us: the promise of the covenant
decisions.reason: The words echo the promises of Deuteronomy for those who obey (Deuteronomy 5:33; 6:3) and of Jeremiah 7:23. The people use them of themselves now; they turn on them in verses 20-22.

decisions.choice: obey
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2). Readable also says "whether we like the answer or not" for "whether good or bad" (m1).

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of ten days, and came [the] word of Yahweh to Jeremiah.
pieces: Ten days later the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah.

L.7: And it came about at the end of ten days that the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Jeremiah.

R.7: Ten days later {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah a message.

decisions.choice: at the end of ten days: the answer came in God's time, not at once
decisions.reason: Jeremiah could not produce an answer on demand; he had to wait until God spoke (compare 28:11-12). The delay also gave the people time, and it shows that the answer did not come from Jeremiah's own opinion.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah (L, B); the LORD gave Jeremiah a message (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah, with Jeremiah's name in place of "me".

records.heading: Stay in the land; do not go to Egypt

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶל־יֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן־קָרֵ֔חַ וְאֶ֛ל כָּל־שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וּלְכָ֨ל־הָעָ֔ם לְמִקָּטֹ֥ן וְעַד־גָּדֽוֹל׃
records.gloss: And he called to Johanan son of Kareah and to all [the] commanders of the forces who [were] with him, and to all the people from small and unto great.
pieces: So he summoned Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him. He summoned all the people as well, from the least to the greatest.

L.8: And he called Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and all the people from the small to the great,

R.8: So Jeremiah called for Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders who were with him. He also called all the people, from the least important to the most important.

decisions.choice: the same people who asked in verse 1
decisions.reason: Jeremiah gathers the same group, from the least to the greatest, so that all who made the request and the oath hear the answer.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (Literal)
decisions.reason: Verse 9 goes on with "and he said to them". Balanced and Readable close the sentence here.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִי֙ אֵלָ֔יו לְהַפִּ֥יל תְּחִנַּתְכֶ֖ם לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: and he said to them: thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, whom you sent me to him to make fall your supplication before him:
pieces: He said to them, "You sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, to lay your plea before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says this:

L.9: and he said to them, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to lay your plea before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:

R.9: He said to them, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says. You sent me to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with your request, and this is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} answer:

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's speech runs from here to the end of the chapter
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks from verse 9 to verse 22. In verses 9-18 he gives God's answer, in which God speaks of himself as "I"; in verses 19-22 he speaks in his own voice and warns them (43:1 says he then finished speaking).

decisions.choice: to lay your plea before him: the same picture as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The people asked that their plea "fall" before Jeremiah (verse 2); here the causative form of the same verb says that Jeremiah made it fall, that is, laid it, before God. He reminds them that the answer is to their own request.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); he says this (B); This is what the LORD ... says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Balanced puts the clause "to whom you sent me" first, so that the long title does not stand between the LORD and "says this". As in 28:16, God's words given by the prophet inside his own speech take no further quotation marks.

decisions.choice: You sent me to him with your request, and this is his answer
decisions.reason: Readable puts the relative clause in a sentence of its own and supplies "this is his answer" to lead into verse 10.

records.source: אִם־שׁ֤וֹב תֵּֽשְׁבוּ֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וּבָנִ֤יתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶהֱרֹ֔ס וְנָטַעְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְלֹ֣א אֶתּ֑וֹשׁ כִּ֤י נִחַ֨מְתִּי֙ אֶל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתִי לָכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: If staying you will stay in the land the this, and I will build you and not I will tear down, and I will plant you and not I will uproot; for I relent concerning the disaster that I have done to you.
pieces: If you will stay in this land, I will build you and not tear you down, and I will plant you and not uproot you, because I relent concerning the disaster I have brought on you.

L.10: If you will indeed stay in this land, then I will build you and not tear [you] down, and I will plant you and not uproot [you]; for I relent concerning the disaster that I have done to you.

R.10: If you stay in this land, I will build you and not tear you down, and I will plant you and not uproot you. The disaster I brought on you grieves me, and I have relented.

decisions.choice: if you will indeed stay: the doubled verb stresses the condition
alternatives: if you will return and stay
decisions.reason: Hebrew strengthens a verb by putting a form of the same verb before it. Here the first word is spelled as if from the verb "return", while the second is "stay". It is best taken as a spelling of the same verb "stay", with one letter dropped, since the whole verse is about remaining in the land (verse 13). Reading it as "return" would give "if you will go back and stay", that is, give up the road to Egypt (41:17).

decisions.choice: build, tear down, plant, uproot: the verbs of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: These are words from 1:10, where Jeremiah is set over the nations "to uproot and to tear down ... to build and to plant". As in 24:6, only building and planting are promised, and tearing down and uprooting are ruled out, but here the promise depends on the people staying in the land.

decisions.choice: I relent concerning the disaster: God grieves over the judgment he has carried out and turns from it
alternatives: I am sorry for the disaster
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 18:8 and 26:3, where God says he will relent from a disaster he has announced. Here the disaster has already happened: the fall of Jerusalem. The verb also carries the sense of being moved to pity or grieved (Judges 2:18; 2 Samuel 24:16). God is not saying that the judgment was wrong (Numbers 23:19), but that he takes no pleasure in it and has now turned from it, so that he can build and plant again.

decisions.choice: build ... and not tear down ... plant ... and not uproot
decisions.reason: The verbs of 1:10 keep their wording at each level, worded as in 24:6. Balanced and Readable join the two halves with "and", as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: grieves me, and I have relented
decisions.reason: In 18:8 and 26:3 Readable says "change my mind" about a disaster not yet sent. Here it has already come, so Readable names both senses of the verb (m3): grief over the disaster and turning from it. "Relented" is kept from Literal and Balanced.

records.source: אַל־תִּֽירְא֗וּ מִפְּנֵי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם יְרֵאִ֖ים מִפָּנָ֑יו אַל־תִּֽירְא֤וּ מִמֶּ֨נּוּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־אִתְּכֶ֣ם אָ֔נִי לְהוֹשִׁ֧יעַ אֶתְכֶ֛ם וּלְהַצִּ֥יל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיָּדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Not be afraid of [the] face of [the] king of Babylon whom you [are] afraid of his face; not be afraid of him, declares Yahweh, for with you [am] I to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
pieces: Do not fear the king of Babylon, though you are afraid of him now. Do not fear him, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am with you, and I will save you and rescue you from his power.

L.11: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid of him, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand.

R.11: Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon. I know you fear him, but do not be afraid of him, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I am with you. I will save you and rescue you from his power.

decisions.choice: the fear of the king of Babylon: they expected him to punish them for the murder of his governor
decisions.reason: Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had set over the land, and the Babylonian soldiers with him (41:2-3). Johanan and the others feared that the king would take revenge on all who were left (41:18).

decisions.choice: I am with you to save you and to deliver you: the promise once given to Jeremiah, now given to the people
decisions.reason: God made the same promise to Jeremiah at his call and when he complained (1:8, 19; 15:20). Now it is offered to the whole remnant, as in 30:10-11, if they stay.

decisions.choice: from his hand: from his power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control.

decisions.choice: his power
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m3). Readable also says "I know you fear him" to keep the repeated fear of the Hebrew in plain words.

records.source: וְאֶתֵּ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם רַחֲמִ֖ים וְרִחַ֣ם אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְהֵשִׁ֥יב אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמַתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will give to you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and he will return you to your soil.
pieces: I will grant you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and let you return to your own land.

L.12: And I will grant you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and bring you back to your own soil.

R.12: I will make the king show you mercy. He will be kind to you and let you go back to your own land.

decisions.choice: I will grant you compassion: I will cause you to find compassion from the king
decisions.reason: To "give someone compassion" is to make others treat him with pity (1 Kings 8:50; Nehemiah 1:11; Psalm 106:46). God will move the king of Babylon to be kind to them.

decisions.choice: he will bring you back, as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "he will cause you to return". Since the people are still in the land, a change of one vowel would give "he will let you stay" (from the verb "stay" in verse 10), and the Greek translation is said to read "I will bring you back". The Hebrew makes sense as it stands: the people had fled from Mizpah and were camped on the road to Egypt (41:16-17), and many had scattered to nearby lands (40:11-12). The king will let them go back to their homes. The description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: your own soil: the farmland of their own homes
decisions.reason: The word is the ground that is farmed, not only the country. It fits the promise to plant them (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the king; be kind to you
decisions.reason: Readable names the king, whom "he" refers to (verse 11), and spreads "compassion" over "mercy" and "kind".

records.source: וְאִם־אֹמְרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לֹ֥א נֵשֵׁ֖ב בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את לְבִלְתִּ֣י שְׁמֹ֔עַ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And if [are] saying you: not we will stay in the land the this, so as not to listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God,
pieces: But suppose you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,

L.13: But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' so as not to listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,

R.13: But you may say, 'We will not stay in this land.' You may refuse to obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: but if you say: the second choice, set against verses 10-12
decisions.reason: Verse 10 began "if you stay"; here begins the other path. The condition runs through verses 13-15, and the result is given in verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: so as not to listen to the voice of the LORD: refusing to obey him
decisions.reason: Saying "we will not stay" would itself be the refusal to obey. The words recall the people's oath in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on through verses 14-16. Readable uses short sentences and picks up the condition again in verse 15.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The words the people might say are quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, which is already in double quotation marks.

records.source: לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹ֚א כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ נָב֔וֹא אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נִרְאֶה֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָ֖ר לֹ֣א נִשְׁמָ֑ע וְלַלֶּ֥חֶם לֹֽא־נִרְעָ֖ב וְשָׁ֥ם נֵשֵֽׁב׃
records.gloss: saying: no, for [the] land of Egypt we will go, where not we will see war, and [the] sound of [the] shofar not we will hear, and for bread not we will hunger, and there we will stay,
pieces: and say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no ram's horn sounding and never go hungry for bread. That is where we will live,'

L.14: saying, 'No, but to the land of Egypt we will go, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread, and there we will stay,'

R.14: You may say, 'No! We will go to Egypt. There we will not see war or hear the trumpet call to battle. We will never be hungry there. That is where we will live.'

decisions.choice: the sound of the shofar: the alarm that warned of an enemy attack
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown to warn of an invading army and to call men to battle (4:5, 19, 21; 6:1). The people want a land where they will never hear it again.

decisions.choice: no, but: a strong refusal followed by the plan they choose instead
decisions.reason: The word "no" answers God's offer to stay, and the next word sets their own plan against it.

decisions.choice: going back to Egypt: turning back the way of the exodus
decisions.reason: Egypt was the land God had brought Israel out of, and the Law warned against going back there (Deuteronomy 17:16; 28:68). The people hope it will be a place of safety and plenty, as it had been in Joseph's time (Genesis 42:1-2). Verses 16-17 answer each of their hopes.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for the shofar, as in Isaiah. Readable adds "call to battle" to say what the sound meant (m1).

decisions.choice: That is where we will live
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "there" first for stress; Balanced and Readable give the stress with a sentence of its own.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אִם־אַ֠תֶּם שׂ֣וֹם תְּשִׂמ֤וּן פְּנֵיכֶם֙ לָבֹ֣א מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבָאתֶ֖ם לָג֥וּר שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: and now, therefore, hear [the] word of Yahweh, remnant of Judah: thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: if you setting will set your faces to go [to] Egypt and you go to sojourn there,
pieces: then hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, remnant of Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: If you are set on going to Egypt, and you go to settle there,

L.15: then now, therefore, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, remnant of Judah. Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: If you indeed set your faces to go to Egypt, and you go to sojourn there,

R.15: If you do that, then listen to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s message, you people who are left from Judah. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: If you have made up your minds to go to Egypt and live there,

decisions.choice: set your faces to go: be determined to go
decisions.reason: To set one's face toward a place is to make up one's mind to go there (2 Kings 12:18; Jeremiah 44:12). The doubled verb stresses how firm the decision is.

decisions.choice: sojourn: live as outsiders in a land not their own
decisions.reason: The verb is used of living somewhere as a resident foreigner, without the rights of a native (Genesis 12:10; 47:4). Israel's fathers had once gone down to sojourn in Egypt; now the people want to do the same.

decisions.choice: and now, therefore: the result of the condition in verses 13-14
decisions.reason: After the long "if" clause the speech turns to what follows, and then restates the condition in God's words before giving the result in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this title in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: sojourn (L); settle (B); live (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for living as an outsider (m2); Balanced and Readable use common words.

decisions.choice: If you do that
decisions.reason: Readable broke verses 13-14 into short sentences, so it supplies these words to pick up the condition again.

records.source: וְהָיְתָ֣ה הַחֶ֗רֶב אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ יְרֵאִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔נָּה שָׁ֛ם תַּשִּׂ֥יג אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָרָעָ֞ב אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֣ם׀דֹּאֲגִ֣ים מִמֶּ֗נּוּ שָׁ֣ם יִדְבַּ֧ק אַחֲרֵיכֶ֛ם מִצְרַ֖יִם וְשָׁ֥ם תָּמֻֽתוּ׃
records.gloss: and it will be, the sword that you [are] afraid of it, there it will overtake you in [the] land of Egypt, and the famine that you [are] anxious about it, there it will cling after you [in] Egypt, and there you will die.
pieces: then the sword you fear will catch up with you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close behind you into Egypt, and you will die there.

L.16: then the sword that you are afraid of will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine that you dread will cling close behind you there in Egypt, and there you will die.

R.16: then the war you are afraid of will catch up with you there in Egypt. The famine you are worried about will follow you there. And you will die there.

decisions.choice: the sword and famine you fear will find you there: they cannot outrun what they flee
decisions.reason: The people wanted to escape war and hunger (verse 14). The very things they fear will go with them to Egypt. "There" is said three times.

decisions.choice: cling after you: pursue you closely and not let go
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick or cling to something; with "after" it describes a pursuer who keeps close behind (1 Samuel 14:22).

decisions.choice: dread: be anxious, worried
decisions.reason: The word describes anxious worry about what may happen (38:19).

decisions.choice: war
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword, as in the wording set for "sword, famine and pestilence" in Jeremiah.

records.source: וְיִֽהְי֣וּ כָל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֨מוּ אֶת־פְּנֵיהֶ֜ם לָב֤וֹא מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם יָמ֕וּתוּ בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ שָׂרִ֣יד וּפָלִ֔יט מִפְּנֵי֙ הָֽרָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י מֵבִ֥יא עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And will be all the men who have set their faces to go [to] Egypt to sojourn there, they will die by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence, and not will be for them a survivor and escapee from before the disaster that I [am] bringing on them.
pieces: All the {{gender:people|men}} who are set on going to Egypt to settle there will die by sword, famine and plague. No one among them will survive or escape the disaster I am bringing on them.

L.17: And all the {{gender:people|men}} who set their faces to go to Egypt to sojourn there will die by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence; and none of them will be a survivor or an escapee from the disaster that I am bringing on them.

R.17: Everyone who is determined to go and live in Egypt will die from war, famine or disease. Not one of them will live through the disaster I will bring on them or escape from it.

decisions.choice: the men: the people as a whole, women and children with them
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "man", but here it means all who go to Egypt; women and children went too (43:6; 44:15).

decisions.choice: they will die: God now speaks of them, not to them
decisions.reason: The speech moves from "you" to "they" and back to "you" in verse 18. The change makes the verse sound like a sentence pronounced over everyone who takes that road.

decisions.choice: survivor or escapee: no one at all will come through
decisions.reason: The two words name one who is left alive and one who gets away. Together they mean that none will escape (44:14; Joshua 8:22).

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (L); sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine or disease (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this list in Jeremiah. Literal keeps "by the" before each word, as the Hebrew does; Readable says "or" because each person dies one way.

decisions.choice: people (default); men (alternative)
decisions.reason: The gender setting, since both sexes are meant (m1). Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting.

records.source: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ נִתַּ֨ךְ אַפִּ֜י וַחֲמָתִ֗י עַל־יֹֽשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כֵּ֣ן תִּתַּ֤ךְ חֲמָתִי֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בְּבֹאֲכֶ֖ם מִצְרָ֑יִם וִהְיִיתֶ֞ם לְאָלָ֤ה וּלְשַׁמָּה֙ וְלִקְלָלָ֣ה וּלְחֶרְפָּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ ע֔וֹד אֶת־הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: just as was poured out my anger and my wrath on [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, so will be poured out my wrath on you when you go [to] Egypt, and you will become an oath-curse and a horror and a curse and a reproach, and not you will see again the place the this.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Just as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury were poured out on the people of Jerusalem, so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become a name used in curses, a horror, a curse and a disgrace, and you will never see this place again.

L.18: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Just as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt; and you will become an execration and a horror, and a curse and a reproach; and you will not see this place again.

R.18: For this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great anger on the people of Jerusalem. In the same way I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you when you go to Egypt. People will use your name when they curse someone. They will be horrified at you, curse you and insult you. You will never see this place again.

decisions.choice: anger and wrath poured out: God's judgment pictured as something poured out like a liquid
decisions.reason: The picture is used of the fall of Jerusalem (7:20; 44:6). The judgment that fell on the city will fall on those who go to Egypt.

decisions.choice: an execration: a name used in an oath of cursing
decisions.reason: The word is a curse spoken as part of an oath. To "become" one means that people will use your fate as the model for a curse, as in 29:22: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab."

decisions.choice: execration, horror, curse, reproach: the covenant curses of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Lists of this kind come from Deuteronomy 28:37 and return in Jeremiah (24:9; 25:18; 29:18; 44:12). They describe a people whose disaster becomes a byword among the nations.

decisions.choice: this place: Judah, their homeland
decisions.reason: The words point to the land where they are standing. Those who go to Egypt will never come back (44:14, 28).

decisions.choice: execration, horror, curse, reproach (L); a name used in curses, a horror, a curse, a disgrace (B); use your name when they curse, horrified, curse, insult (R)
decisions.reason: "Horror" and "curse" follow the wording set for these lists in Jeremiah; "reproach" and "disgrace" follow 24:9. Readable turns the nouns into what people will do.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies ... says this (B); This is what the LORD of Armies ... says (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

records.source: דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה עֲלֵיכֶם֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אַל־תָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יִם יָדֹ֨עַ֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּ כִּי־הַעִידֹ֥תִי בָכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Has spoken Yahweh to you, remnant of Judah: not go [to] Egypt. Knowing know that I have warned you the day.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has told you, remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for certain that I have warned you today.

L.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to you, remnant of Judah: 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for certain that I have warned you this day.

R.19: You people who are left from Judah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told you, 'Do not go to Egypt.' You can be sure of this: I have warned you today.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah now speaks in his own voice
decisions.reason: God's answer ended in verse 18. In verses 19-22 Jeremiah sums it up and warns them, speaking of God as "the LORD" and of himself as "I".

decisions.choice: I have warned you: I have testified against you as a witness
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word "witness". The people called on the LORD as a witness against them (verse 5); now Jeremiah has solemnly warned them, and his warning will stand as evidence against them (Deuteronomy 8:19).

decisions.choice: know for certain: the doubled verb stresses the warning
decisions.reason: As in verse 22. It means "make no mistake".

decisions.choice: You people who are left from Judah
decisions.reason: Readable puts the address first and explains "remnant".

records.source: כִּ֣י הִתְעֵיתֶם֮בְּנַפְשֽׁוֹתֵיכֶם֒ כִּֽי־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֗י אֶל־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲדֵ֔נוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וּכְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֜ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ כֵּ֥ן הַגֶּד־לָ֖נוּ וְעָשִֽׂינוּ׃
records.gloss: For you have led astray yourselves at the cost of your lives; for you sent me to Yahweh your God, saying: pray for us to Yahweh our God, and according to all that will say Yahweh our God, so tell to us, and we will do.
pieces: You have deceived yourselves, and it will cost you your lives. You yourselves sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and said, 'Pray for us to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. Tell us everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, and we will do it.'

L.20: For you have led yourselves astray at the cost of your lives; for you yourselves sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, saying, 'Pray for us to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, so tell us, and we will do [it].'

R.20: You have fooled yourselves, and it will cost you your lives. You sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You said, 'Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God for us. Tell us everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, and we will do it.'

decisions.choice: you have led yourselves astray at the cost of your lives
alternatives: you have gone astray at the cost of your lives
you acted deceitfully in your hearts
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) of the verb differ slightly from the form the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere); both come from a verb meaning "to wander" or, in this form, "to lead astray". The verb usually has an object, and here the phrase after it can mean "against yourselves" or "at the cost of your lives". So the clause may mean that they misled themselves to their own ruin, that they made a fatal mistake, or that they were not honest when they made their oath. Each gives the same warning: their choice will cost them their lives.

decisions.choice: your God ... our God: Jeremiah repeats their own words back to them
decisions.reason: Jeremiah says they sent him to "the LORD your God" and quotes them saying "the LORD our God" (verse 6). They claimed the LORD as their own God but would not do what he said.

decisions.choice: for you yourselves sent me: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: The word "you" is written out for emphasis. The request was theirs; they cannot now treat the answer as Jeremiah's idea (43:2-3).

decisions.choice: deceived yourselves (B); fooled yourselves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the first sense in m1 and say "it will cost you your lives" for the phrase after the verb.

records.source: וָאַגִּ֥ד לָכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם וְלֹ֣א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֗ם בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וּלְכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I have told you the day, and not you have listened to [the] voice of Yahweh your God and in all that he has sent me to you.
pieces: Today I have told you, yet you have not obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in anything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent me to tell you.

L.21: And I have told you this day, but you have not listened to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in anything that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent me to you [with].

R.21: I have told you today. But you have not obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You have not done any of the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent me to tell you.

decisions.choice: you have not listened: Jeremiah speaks of their refusal as already made
decisions.reason: The people do not reply until 43:2-3, but Jeremiah already sees their answer. His words describe what they have decided in their hearts, and the next chapter shows he was right.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice: obeyed
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, where they promised to listen to the voice of the LORD.

decisions.choice: obeyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2). Literal supplies "with" to finish the phrase "sent me to you".

records.gloss: And now knowing know that by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence you will die in the place that you desire to go to sojourn there.
pieces: So now know for certain that you will die by sword, famine and plague in the place where you want to go and settle."

L.22: And now know for certain that by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence you will die in the place where you desire to go to sojourn."

R.22: So now you can be sure of this: you will die from war, famine or disease in the place where you want to go and live."

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence: the same three as in verse 17
decisions.reason: Jeremiah ends with the sentence God gave in verse 17. The place they long for will be the place of their death.

decisions.choice: desire: want, take pleasure in
decisions.reason: The verb means to delight in or set one's heart on something. It shows that their minds are made up.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (L); sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine or disease (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17. Literal keeps the Hebrew order, with the three words before the verb.

decisions.choice: closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's speech, opened in verse 9, ends here (43:1).
